_about: A phrasal verb is a verb lemma plus a particle ('spin up', 'kick off'). The style
standard 4.1 rule 5 makes a phrasal verb in prose a failure. There is no reliable
POS route, so this list is the detector. It is a maintained repo asset.
Each entry is one verb lemma plus one particle. The rule matches the lemma in its
regular inflected forms too (base, -s/-es/-ies, -ing, -ed). A verb with an irregular
form (a doubled consonant, an irregular past, an irregular participle) lists that form
in 'irregular'. A regular verb omits the field.
This seed comes from the phrasal verbs the style standard 4.1 rule 5 names and the
ASD-STE100 skill lists (SKILL.md 'Soft phrasal verbs', before-after.md). Grow the list
as a new false negative appears (SPEC 2.3). Add the lemma, the particle, and any
irregular form. Precision is moderate by design: the list catches its entries, misses
an entry not on it, and may over-flag a literal use ('reach out your hand' reads the
same as 'reach out to the team').
